summary: Georg Morgenstierne (1892–1978) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin under Sten Konow, Hermann Jacobi, Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Beckh, and Wilhelm Schulze, later teaching at Oslo and Gothenburg.

Linguist Georg Renatus Solta (1919–2005) earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (1934–1939), where he studied under Paul Kretschmer and Wilhelm Havers. He spent his career at the University of Vienna as Privatdozent (1953) and ao. Professor (1967).
Georg Simmel (1858–1918) was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1876–1881). He later held an academic post there from around 1885 to 1914.

Philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel (1770–1831) studied at Tübingen (under F. W. J. Schelling) and Jena. His career included posts at the University of Jena (1800–1806), Aegidianum Nürnberg (1808–1816), Heidelberg University (~1816–1818), and the University of Berlin (1818–1831).

Georg von Simson (b. 1933) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Mainz and Göttingen (Ph.D. under Ernst Waldschmidt) and held positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977) and the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz (1840–1893) worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology. He studied at Jena, Halle-Wittenberg (under August Friedrich Pott), TU Dresden, and Leipzig. He was later professor at Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889).

Sinologist and linguist George A. Kennedy (1901–1960) studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1935) under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke. He subsequently held a faculty post at Yale University from ~1935 to 1960.

George A. Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and UCLA (Ph.D. under Robert E. Buswell Jr.) and held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (2001) and University of Saskatchewan (2011).

Linguist and Indologist George Abraham Grierson (1851–1941) studied at Trinity College Dublin under Robert Atkinson, Cambridge, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served in the Indian Civil Service, directed the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and headed SOAS University of London (1917–1925).

George Adolphus Jacob (1840–1918) was an Indologist educated at Sheffield Collegiate School. He served in the Indian Army and Bombay Staff Corps (~1857–1888), was Acting Superintendent at Native Army School, Poona (1862–1865), and became a Fellow at Mumbai University.

George Baumann (b. 1936) is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (~1968–1973) and trained at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut Nordrhein-Westfalen. He served at the University of Tübingen and as Bibliotheksreferendar at Tübingen University Library from 1976 to 2001.

George Bidie (1830–1913) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at the University of Edinburgh and Marischal College, Aberdeen, he served as Professor of Botany at Madras Medical College (1866–1870) and Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (1872–1884).
George Bogle (1746–1781) was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who completed his education at Enfield Academy and the University of Edinburgh.

George Bosworth Burch (1902–1973) specialized in philosophy and Indology, studying at Harvard, Geneva, and Paris. He held professorships at the College of Idaho (1942–1946) and Tufts University (1946–1967), alongside visiting posts at Indian Institute of Philosophy and Visva-Bharati University.
George Byres Mainwaring (1825–1893) was an Indologist and linguist who served in the Bengal Army beginning in 1842 and reached the rank of Lieutenant-Colonel in the Bengal Staff Corps in 1868.

George C. O. Haas (1883–1964) was an Indologist who completed his A.B. and Ph.D. at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson. He taught German at City College of New York (1904–1916) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

George Campbell (1824–1892) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He received his education at Hamilton Academy, Edinburgh Academy, Madras College, the University of St Andrews, East India Company College, and the University of Oxford.

George Cardona (1936–2024) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at NYU and Yale under Paul Thieme and Warren Crawford Cowgill, alongside traditional Indian scholars, and had a long career as Professor of Linguistics at the University of Pennsylvania (1965–2007).
George Carstairs (1880–1948) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at The Albany Academy and the University of Glasgow, where he earned an M.A. (~1897–1901) and a D.D. (~1935).

George Chatalian (1920–1997) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Brown University and Harvard University (Ph.D. 1968). He held academic posts at Franklin Pierce University, the University of Lagos, and Obafemi Awolowo University (1983).
